key_insight: Adjoint-augmented pseudo-arclength continuation directly tracks the absolute/convective instability boundary as a neutral stationary-saddle manifold, avoiding repeated complex-wavenumber and parameter scans.
engineering_relevance: This gives a much faster and more robust way to map instability thresholds in aerodynamics and fluid systems, especially for large non-normal eigenvalue problems with folds or re-entrant boundaries.
method: Formulate the zero-group-velocity condition as an adjoint solvability residual.
Solve direct and adjoint eigenproblems together with complex gauge and neutral-growth constraints.
Use scaled pseudo-arclength continuation to follow the boundary through parameter folds without switching continuation variables.
evidence_signal: The method matches analytical and finite-difference benchmarks to about 1e-8 relative critical Reynolds number and reduces wall time by roughly 14.0x to 30.6x versus nested scanning.
watch_item: The approach still depends on correct eigenpair/branch association and careful implementation of the coupled direct-adjoint continuation system.
paper_title: Tracking the boundary between absolute/convective instability using adjoint equations
